ip.context: Energy loss expressed as a height of water column. Appears in Darcy-Weisbach, Hazen-Williams, Manning pipe, and Penstock calculators. Distinct from 'pressure drop' — use the hydraulic engineering term.

The current 'губитак напора / gubitak tlačne visine' (= loss of hydraulic head) is more precise in a hydraulic engineering context and is preferred. mhp.context: Total elevation difference between the headpond water surface and the turbine — before subtracting penstock losses. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator.
mhp.translation_notes: 'Gross' means total/before-deduction. Pair with 'net head' for clarity. Use the hydro-power standard term.

mhp.context: Effective head available at the turbine after subtracting penstock friction and minor losses from gross head. H_net = H_gross - h_L.
mhp.translation_notes: 'Net' means after-deduction. Pair with 'gross head'. Use the hydro-power standard term. WMO No. 385 entry 111 ('available head') gives the Russian term 'полезный напор' (useful head) / syn. 'располагаемый напор' — these overlap with net head in Russian hydro engineering practice.

mhp.context: Overall efficiency of a micro-hydro power plant — product of turbine, generator, and transmission efficiencies. Dimensionless, 0–1. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator.
mhp.translation_notes: 'Plant' here means the power plant/installation, not a living plant. Use the energy/electrical engineering term for overall system efficiency. 2026-07-13 reconciliation pass (roadmap item 42): glossary updated to match incumbent, internally-consistent lang-file usage discovered by 5 independent category-5-wave-1 translation agents (it, pt, ru, tr) — glossary values were stale, not the shipped files.

mhp.context: Energy loss expressed as a height of water column. Appears in Darcy-Weisbach, Hazen-Williams, Manning pipe, and Penstock calculators. Distinct from 'pressure drop' — use the hydraulic engineering term.

The current 'губитак напора / gubitak tlačne visine' (= loss of hydraulic head) is more precise in a hydraulic engineering context and is preferred. mhp.context: A hydropower configuration that uses natural river flow without a dam or significant storage reservoir. Power output varies with seasonal river flow. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator.
mhp.translation_notes: Use the established energy/hydropower sector term. 'Run' means natural river current — do not translate as jogging or running. mhp.context: The intake structure at the upstream end of a penstock or canal, where water is diverted from the river or reservoir into the conveyance system. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator (penstock diameter and length descriptions).

Russian: 'водозаборное сооружение'. German: 'Einlaufbauwerk'. In many languages, 'intake structure' is preferred over a literal translation of 'headworks'.

mhp.context: Energy loss at pipe junctions, bends, fittings, and entrance — a local (point) loss as opposed to distributed friction loss along the pipe. h_m = k_m × v²/(2g). Appears in Manning Pipe Head Loss and Micro-Hydro Power calculators.

The term 'minor' is conventional but misleading — do not imply these losses are always small; the parenthetical '(local)' carries the true sense. Use the hydraulic engineering term for local/point losses at fittings. French: 'perte singulière'. Spanish: 'pérdida local' or 'pérdida por accesorio'. Russian: 'местные потери'. Chinese: '局部水头损失'. mhp.context: Local head loss at fittings/valves/couplers (coefficient k_m). Canonical merged concept for the former 'junction loss' (mphl_) and 'minor loss' (mhp_/ip_). Manning Pipe Head Loss, Micro-Hydro Power, Irrigation Pressure.
mhp.translation_notes: CANONICAL ENGLISH LABEL: "Minor (local) loss" (label-normalization decision, item 90, 2026-07-07). 'Minor ⇄ local' — a local/point loss at fittings, NOT a "smaller" loss; the '(local)' parenthetical fixes the mistranslation trap. Symbol h_m, coefficient k_m (lowercase h reserved for loss components; capital H reserved for total/gross/net head, per the same decision). am ADDED (2026-07-10, category-3 am re-translation): 'ጥቃቅን (አካባቢያዊ) ኪሳራ' (tiqaqin (akababiyawi) kisara) mirrors the English structure word-for-word — 'ጥቃቅን' (minor/small) followed by the parenthetical '(አካባቢያዊ)' (local, i.e. of a specific place/area) — so the same mistranslation-blocking device English uses (the '(local)' qualifier preventing a 'smaller loss' misreading) is preserved in Amharic rather than silently dropped. Replaces the prior am file's 'የማያያዣ ኪሳራ' (connector/joint loss), which named the physical fitting rather than the local/point-loss concept. km ADDED (2026-07-10, category-3 km re-translation): 'ការបាត់បង់មូលដ្ឋាន' (local-basis loss) reuses មូលដ្ឋាន ('local', already established suite-wide for this exact merged concept in ip_km's tooltip 'មេគុណបាត់បង់មូលដ្ឋានសរុប' = 'total local-loss coefficient'), so category-3 now converges on the same word ip_ already uses rather than coining a second competing term. Deliberately avoids 'តូច' (small), sidestepping the minor⇄smaller mistranslation trap the English '(local)' parenthetical exists to block. Replaces the km file's prior mphl_junction_loss value 'ការបាត់បង់ junction' (untranslated English word left in place). ps ADDED (2026-07-10, category-3 ps wave-3 re-translation): 'ځایی ضیاع' (local loss) uses ځایی (local/positional) + the established ps loss word ضیاع, following the majority pattern already set by ar/fa/es/fr/hr/id/it/ro/ru/sr/tr/uk/ur/zh — all of which render this concept as 'local loss' alone rather than translating 'minor' literally, since the '(local)' qualifier is the operative disambiguator, not 'minor'. Deliberately avoids a word for 'small/minor' (e.g. کوچنی) to sidestep the same minor⇄smaller trap the English parenthetical exists to block. Replaces the prior ps file's 'د جنکشن ضیاع' (junction loss — the pre-consolidation, pre-item-90 term) and fixes its symbol from capital H_m to lowercase h_m. keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_2_def: Tanks, water quality, and control valves that open and close on their own (PRV, PSV, FCV) are not modeled. A pipe can carry a fixed minor loss, but not a valve whose open or closed state depends on the flow being solved for.
keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_3_def: Every project is a tab, and every tab is saved in this browser as you work. Clearing your browser data deletes them all, so keep your work in a file: File, Save as. When a project file is kept on a shared drive, this page tells you if a colleague already has it open, so that two people do not write over each other. Because this is an early preview, please use it for small networks and for testing only.
keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_5_def: A pump follows H = H₀ − aQ^b, where H is the head the pump adds and Q is the flow through it. Enter one, two, or three points from the manufacturer's curve. Three points — the head at zero flow, the normal working point, and the point of highest flow — fit H₀, a and b directly, and follow a published curve most closely. Two points fit a parabola (b = 2) with its peak at zero flow. One point uses a common rule: the head at zero flow is 1.33 × the head you enter, and the highest flow is 2 × the flow you enter, which again gives b = 2. A pump with no points entered adds no head at all. The curve is not stopped at zero, so asking a pump for more flow than its curve can deliver gives a negative head. The fix is a bigger pump or a smaller demand, not a different curve fit.
keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_4_def: Scenarios, so that one project can hold several sets of demands. Tables of node and pipe results. Opening a file you used recently without hunting for it again. keys.lpn_status_already_open: That file is already open here as {name}, so this switched to it rather than opening a second copy.
keys.lpn_status_already_open_dirty: That file is already open here as {name}, with changes you have not saved to it. This switched to it rather than opening a second copy. Use File, Revert if you want the version on disk instead.
keys.lpn_close_save_prompt: Save your changes to {name} before closing it?
keys.lpn_close_browser_prompt: {name} is kept only in this browser. If you close it without saving it to a file, it is gone for good.
keys.lpn_revert_confirm: Throw away the changes you have made and load {file} again from the disk?
keys.lpn_file_needs_reopen: This project came from {file}, but the connection to that file has been lost. Choose the file again to connect to it.
keys.lpn_file_write_failed: Could not write to the file. It may have been moved or renamed, or permission may have been withdrawn. Your work is still saved in this browser. Use Save to file to choose the file again.
keys.lpn_file_changed_elsewhere: Somebody else has saved to this file since you opened it, so saving now would write over their work. Use File, Save as to keep your changes in a file of your own, or File, Revert to throw yours away and load theirs.

keys.lpn_lock_open_heading_times: {name} has this file open; the last edit was {x} ago, {y} after the last save.
keys.lpn_lock_open_heading_unsaved: {name} has this file open; the last edit was {x} ago, and none of it has been saved to this file yet.
keys.lpn_lock_open_heading_saved: {name} has this file open; the last edit was {x} ago, and their work is saved to the file.
keys.lpn_lock_open_heading_seen: {name} has this file open but has not edited it. Their browser last checked in {x} ago.
keys.lpn_lock_open_choices: Your choices: (1) Cancel and ask them to open it if necessary and then close it properly (closing the browser does not close the project), (2) Open read-only, or (3) if all else fails, you can break their lock. Their unsaved work is not lost, but they will not be able to save over your changes, and somebody may have to merge the two by hand.
keys.lpn_lock_readonly_banner: Read-only: {name} has this file open. You can change anything you like here, but you cannot save. Use File, Save as to save to a different file.
keys.lpn_lock_unavailable: Beware: could not reach the server to check or create a lock on this project, so nothing is stopping a colleague from editing the same file at the same time. You will be told if locking starts working again.
keys.lpn_lock_storage_error: Beware: this site cannot save lock records, so nothing is stopping a colleague from editing the same file at the same time. This is a setup fault on the server, not something you can fix here — the lock folder is not writable by the web server.
keys.lpn_lock_full_error: Beware: this site has run out of room to record who has which project open, so nothing is stopping a colleague from editing the same file at the same time. This is a setup fault on the server, not something you can fix here.
keys.lpn_lock_not_asked: Locking is not running for this project, so nothing is stopping a colleague from editing the same file at the same time. This browser has no name recorded for you yet, or the project has no identifier — saving the project to a file sets both.
keys.lpn_lock_restored: Locking is working again, and this file is now yours to save to.
keys.lpn_file_training_1: Your project will be saved in a file on this computer. It is saved when you ask, and at no other time, so nothing is written to that file behind your back.
keys.lpn_file_training_2: So that two people never edit one file at the same time, this site keeps track of who has it open. If somebody already has it, you can still open it and look, or keep a copy of your own.
keys.lpn_file_training_permission: The first time you save, your browser will ask whether this site may edit the file. That question comes from the browser, not from us, and saying yes is what lets Save write your work back. It is usually asked only once per file.
keys.lpn_file_training_3: Give a short name your colleagues will know you by. Your initials are ideal. Anyone who opens the same file can see it, so do not use anything private.
keys.lpn_file_reconnect_prompt: This project came from {file}. Your browser needs your permission again before it can write to it. Reconnect below.
keys.lpn_saveas_same_file: That is the same file somebody else has open, so it cannot be saved over. Choose a different file or a different name.
keys.lpn_saveas_overwrites_project: That file already holds a different project, {name}. Saving here replaces it completely. Continue?
keys.lpn_saveas_overwrites_newer: That file has changed since you last saw it, so somebody else has almost certainly saved to it. Saving here replaces their version with yours. Continue?
keys.lpn_status_closed_empty: Closed {closed}. Started a new empty project.
keys.lpn_storage_full: Not saved. Browser storage is full or unavailable, so your recent changes will be lost when you close this tab.
keys.lpn_notes_1_def: Solves one set of demands at a time, using the same gradient method EPANET uses. It does not model how the network changes over time.
keys.lpn_notes_2_def: Tanks, water quality, and control valves that open and close on their own (PRV, PSV, FCV) are not modeled. A pipe can carry a fixed minor loss, but not a valve whose open or closed state depends on the flow being solved for.
keys.lpn_notes_3_def: Every project is a tab, and every tab is saved in this browser as you work. Clearing your browser data deletes them all, so keep your work in a file: File, Save as. An asterisk on a tab means it holds changes that are not in a file. Nothing is ever written to a file unless you ask. In some browsers a project connects to the file you save it to, and File, Save writes back to that same file from then on; in others no connection is possible, so Save is disabled and only Save as is available. When a project file is kept on a shared drive, this page tells you if a colleague already has it open, so that two people do not write over each other. Because this is an early preview, please use it for small networks and for testing only.
keys.lpn_notes_5_def: A pump follows H = H₀ − aQ^b, where H is the head the pump adds and Q is the flow through it. Enter one, two, or three points from the manufacturer's curve. Three points — the head at zero flow, the normal working point, and the point of highest flow — fit H₀, a and b directly, and follow a published curve most closely. Two points fit a parabola (b = 2) with its peak at zero flow. One point uses a common rule: the head at zero flow is 1.33 × the head you enter, and the highest flow is 2 × the flow you enter, which again gives b = 2. A pump with no points entered adds no head at all. The curve is not stopped at zero, so asking a pump for more flow than its curve can deliver gives a negative head. The fix is a bigger pump or a smaller demand, not a different curve fit.
keys.lpn_notes_4_def: Scenarios, so that one project can hold several sets of demands. Tables of node and pipe results. Opening a file you used recently without hunting for it again. Reading and writing EPANET .inp files. Other languages: this page is in English only for now. Comments and suggestions are always welcome (see the feedback link above).
keys.lpn_notes_epanet_def: In August 2026 the Hazen-Williams coefficient and exponent were changed to match EPANET. Head loss results differ from earlier versions of this page by up to 0.1 percent, which is far smaller than the uncertainty in the C value itself.
keys.lpn_id_invalid: Enter an ID with no spaces and no quotation marks.
keys.lpn_id_taken: That ID is already in use.
keys.lpn_diag_no_fixed_head: Add a reservoir. The network needs at least one known water level before it can be solved.
keys.lpn_diag_dangling_link: A pipe or pump connects to a node that no longer exists:
keys.lpn_diag_unreachable: These nodes have no path to a reservoir:
keys.lpn_diag_not_converged: No solution was found. Check for values that cannot be real, such as a diameter of zero.
keys.lpn_field_roughness_tip: Hazen-Williams C. A higher number means a smoother pipe: about 150 for new plastic, 130 for new steel or iron, and 100 for old pipe.
keys.lpn_field_length_tip: Length of the pipe. With Auto turned on this follows what you drew. Turn Auto off to type a length that differs from the drawing.
keys.lpn_field_km_tip: Loss from the bends, valves, and fittings on this pipe, counted as a multiple of the velocity head. Use 0 for a plain straight pipe.
keys.lpn_pump_curve_ref_note: Using the curve entered for pump {id}.
keys.lpn_pump_curve_note: One, two, or three points — see "Pump curve" in the Notes below.
keys.lpn_mode_select: Mode: Select. Click an element or a label to see or change it. Drag to move a node, a vertex, or a label. Double-click a pipe to add or remove a vertex.
keys.lpn_mode_delete: Mode: Delete. Click an element to remove it.
keys.lpn_mode_add_junction: Mode: Add Junction. Click the map to place a junction. Switch to Select mode to change or move elements and labels.
keys.lpn_mode_add_reservoir: Mode: Add Reservoir. Click the map to place a reservoir. Switch to Select mode to change or move elements and labels.
keys.lpn_mode_add_pipe: Mode: Add Pipe. Click a node, then another node, to connect them. Switch to Select mode to change or move elements and labels.
keys.lpn_mode_add_pump: Mode: Add Pump. Click a node, then another node, to connect them. Switch to Select mode to change or move elements and labels.
keys.lpn_mode_add_text: Mode: Add Text. Click the map to place a text label. Click near a node to attach the text to that node. Switch to Select mode to change or move elements and labels.
keys.lpn_tip_select: Use this mode to change, move, and drag things on the map.
keys.lpn_tip_labels_draggable: You can drag a label to move it. Double-click a label to put it back.
keys.lpn_labels_decimals_tip: Decimal places shown for this label
keys.lpn_backdrop_scale_prompt1: Click two points on the background image, such as the two ends of a bar scale. Then type the real distance between them.
keys.lpn_backdrop_scale_prompt2: Real distance between the two points
keys.lpn_backdrop_position_prompt1: Click any point on the background image. This is the point you will move.
keys.lpn_backdrop_position_prompt2: Choose where that point should go, then click Continue.
keys.lpn_backdrop_coords_prompt: Type the X,Y that point should move to
keys.lpn_settings_defaults_note: Used for elements you create from now on. Existing elements are not changed.
keys.lpn_settings_push_note: Only the properties whose labels are showing right now are applied.
keys.lpn_push_confirm: Replace these properties on every existing element with the current default inputs? Values you have typed will be overwritten. You can undo this.
keys.lpn_push_none_displayed: No default input is showing as a label right now, so there is nothing to apply. Turn on the labels for the properties you want in the Labels panel, then try again.
keys.lpn_push_nothing: No existing element has any of the properties being applied.
keys.lpn_push_no_change: Every element already has these values, so nothing would change.
keys.lpn_settings_tolerance_tip: How close the solver has to get before it stops. A smaller number is more exact and takes longer.
keys.lpn_settings_map_height_tip: On a small screen the map is drawn shorter than this, so that part of the page is always left to scroll.
keys.lpn_confirm_restore_defaults: Reset all settings (ID prefixes, default inputs, solver settings, map display, legend position, and visible labels) to their defaults? Your network is not changed. Settings belong to the open project, so your other projects keep their own.
keys.lpn_confirm_wipe: Delete EVERYTHING saved for this page — every project, every background image, all settings, and your unit choices — and reload the page as a brand-new visitor would see it? This cannot be undone.
